```{=typst}
#set par(justify: false)
#set text(hyphenate: false)
#show raw: set text(font: "Fira Code")
// software names: monospace + deep blue, except inside code chunks
// (sized by the inline raw rule below)
#let in-code = state("in-code", false)
#show regex("\\b(txomics/tapir|tximeta|tximport|plyxp|tidySE|splicelogic|treeClust|tapir|TAPIR|plyranges|tidyomics|salmon|oarfish|bambu|DESeq2|satuRn)\\b"): it => context {
  if in-code.get() { it } else { text(fill: rgb("#2B6CA3"), raw(it.text)) }
}
// inline code in slide text: scale up from raw's 0.8em (not inside chunks)
#show raw.where(block: false): it => context {
  if in-code.get() { it } else { text(size: 1.15em, it) }
}
// per-slide overrides: #code-size.update(20pt), #code-width.update(70%)
#let code-size = state("code-size", 24pt)
#let code-width = state("code-width", 100%)
// per-slide brackets right of a chunk: #code-brackets.update(((1, 10, "A"), ...))
// with (first line, last line, label); reset to none after the chunk
#let code-brackets = state("code-brackets", none)
#let code-bracket(h, label) = {
  let c = rgb("#13294B")
  let s = 1.5pt + c
  stack(dir: ltr, spacing: 0.3cm,
    box(width: 0.35cm, height: h, stroke: (top: s, right: s, bottom: s)),
    box(height: h, align(horizon, text(size: 18pt, fill: c, label))))
}
#let Skylighting(fill: none, number: false, start: 1, sourcelines) = {
  in-code.update(true)
  context {
    let sz = code-size.get()
    set text(size: sz)
    set par(leading: 0.5em)
    let blocks = []
    for ln in sourcelines { blocks = blocks + ln + EndLine() }
    let br = code-brackets.get()
    if br == none {
      block(fill: rgb("#f1f3f5"), width: code-width.get(), inset: 6pt,
        radius: 3pt, breakable: false, blocks)
    } else {
      // height of source lines a..b (1-based, inclusive) as rendered
      let H(a, b) = measure({
        set text(size: sz)
        set par(leading: 0.5em)
        sourcelines.slice(a - 1, b).join(EndLine())
      }).height
      let aside = box(width: 4cm, {
        for (a, b, label) in br {
          let y = if a == 1 { 0pt } else { H(1, a) - H(a, a) }
          place(top + left, dy: 6pt + y - 2pt,
            code-bracket(H(a, b) + 4pt, label))
        }
      })
      grid(columns: (code-width.get(), auto), column-gutter: 0.3cm,
        block(fill: rgb("#f1f3f5"), width: 100%, inset: 6pt,
          radius: 3pt, breakable: false, blocks),
        aside)
    }
  }
  in-code.update(false)
}
#let sticker-img(name, h) = image("images/" + name + ".png", height: h)
// corner sticker: same gap (0.7cm) from the page's top and right edges;
// dx/dy are relative to the content area (margins x: 2.8cm, y: 1.2cm)
```

# Why new syntax (for humans or LLMs)?

```{=typst}
#let detail(body) = text(size: 16pt, fill: luma(110), body)
#{
  set enum(spacing: 1em)
  set par(leading: 0.5em)
  [
    1. Humans read and review code (for now) \
      #detail[Concise and easy to comprehend]
    2. Grammar enables precision while maintaining readability, e.g. \
      #detail[“find peaks near DE genes” vs. \
      \
      `genes |> filter(de) |> promoters(...) |> join_overlap_inner(peaks, ...)`]
    3. Composable verbs map meaningfully to many analyses \
      #detail[With standard data classes, catches silent bookkeeping & genomics errors]
    4. Tested, maintained verbs safer than freshly generated code \
      #detail[Same verbs work consistently across backends]
  ]
}
```

# A grammar for annotated matrices

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#place(top + right, dx: 2.8cm - 0.7cm - 3.1cm, dy: 0.7cm - 1.2cm,
  sticker-img("tidyomics", 3cm))
#student("justinlandis", "Justin Landis")
#align(center, image("images/plyxp-bindings.png", height: 9cm))
// context colors: rows purple, cols dark orange, assays dark green
#let c-rows(s) = text(fill: rgb("#6A3D9A"), raw(s))
#let c-cols(s) = text(fill: rgb("#D2691E"), raw(s))
#let c-assays(s) = text(fill: rgb("#2E7D32"), raw(s))
#align(center, box(align(left)[
  #set text(size: 16pt)
  - plyxp brings _dplyr_ verbs to annotated matrices, efficiently
  - Expressions are scoped to contexts: #c-assays("assays"), #c-rows("rows()"), or #c-cols("cols()")
  - Pronouns #c-assays(".assays"), #c-rows(".rows"), #c-cols(".cols") reach across contexts
  - We are looking to support _AnnData_
]))
```

# plyxp: mutate, filter, aggregate

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
xp <- new_plxyp(se) |>
  mutate(
    scaled_cts = counts / .cols$size_factor,
    rows(ave = map_dbl(.assays$scaled_cts, mean))
  ) |>
  filter(rows(ave > 10), cols(batch != "b3"))

# also: rowMeans(.assays_asis$scaled_cts)

genes <- xp |>
  group_by(rows(gene_id)) |>
  summarize(counts = colSums(counts))
```

# FP control for aggregation: count splitting

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#code-size.update(16pt)
#code-width.update(60%)
// split1/split2 share a pixel scale (-1..1 = 680px); zero line at px 463 vs 381,
// so split1 is 840/768 as wide and the others are padded left by 82px;
// split1 gets 10px right padding since the stack right-aligns its children
#let k = 8cm / 768
#place(horizon + right, dx: -1cm, dy: 1.15cm,
  stack(spacing: 0.2cm,
    pad(right: 10 * k, image("images/split1.png", width: 840 * k)),
    pad(left: 82 * k, image("images/split2.png", width: 768 * k)),
    pad(left: 82 * k, image("images/split3.png", width: 768 * k))))
// shift the (vertically centered) code down to match the plots' dy
#v(1.6cm)
```

Aggregate counts from similar transcripts:

```{r}
#| eval: false
split <- xp |>
  mutate(train = rbinom(n(), counts, 0.5),
         test = counts - train)

tree <- split |>
  group_by(rows(gene_id)) |>
  mutate(rows(nodes = exons |> cluster_data()))

inner_nodes <- tree |>
  group_by_nodes(rows(inner_nodes(nodes))) |>
  summarize(across(everything(), colSums))
```

# splicelogic: events as composable ranges

```{=typst}
#sticker("splicelogic")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
# <ranges> to <ranges>: "endomorphic"
events <- exons |> find_all_events()

skipped <- exons |>
  find_skipped_exons() |>
  flank_upstream(100) %>%
  mutate(intron_seq = get_seq(., "hg38"))

# results attached to ranges as columns
skipped$intron_seq
```

```{r}
exons |>
  preprocess(...,
    additional_columns = ...)
```

# Back to the question: why new syntax?

```{=typst}
#align(center, image("images/finally.jpg", height: 5.5cm))
```

- tximeta: provenance travels with the data
- plyxp: _dplyr_ verbs on standard objects
- splicelogic: ranges in, ranges out: composes with plyranges
- Tested verbs and classes handle the bookkeeping
